statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls to 7 of 100 in the low band, eighteen points below the 25 block threshold, because the CME weekend halt removes the price path this score measures, while stress stays at 68 in the high band on carried exposure and confidence is 89 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support the reading. First, the completed Friday path granted mean reversion: the cash index closed 29,368.44, up 0.91% but 105 points below its 29,473.12 high, and NQ's final tick of 29,391.75 was 108 points under a 29,499.50 high that had capped the contract since midday. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, beyond the end of this horizon, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No danger window is named, because a narrow evidence-based window requires an open tape and none exists inside the horizon. Stress is the elevated series rather than tail: it opens at 68 and decays to a weekend baseline near 44, a floor set above the level used before the close because carried exposure now includes the precautionary shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, roughly 7 million barrels per day of Hormuz-bypass capacity with no published restart timeline, alongside a rate decision that is close to fully priced. Tail remains far below the block threshold throughout.
headline: A closed tape after an orderly close: NDX finished 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but 105 points below its high, NQ's last tick before the 21:00 UTC halt was 29,391.75, and the weekend now carries an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage into a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement throughout. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range, finishing 105 points below its own high so the closing auction did not extend the advance. NQ futures printed a final tick of 29,391.75, up 0.88%, some 108 points under a 29,499.50 session high, inside a 29,040.50 to 29,499.50 range. Participation was broad rather than narrow, with delayed cross-asset context showing all eight tracked megacaps positive and semiconductors higher, led by technology and communication services. Broad participation supports direction but is not by itself evidence of a no-retracement path.

Both dated United States releases for the day are verified and behind the market. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, while core rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above consensus, and 2.4% over the year. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% and the longer-run measure at 3.4%. Futures-implied odds of a quarter-point increase at Wednesday's decision moved to roughly 87% from about 72% before the print.

Cross-asset signals were partial rather than uniformly aligned. Volatility collapsed, with VIX closing 15.84 after an 11.2% decline in a 15.59 to 17.71 range. Front-end yields rose, the two-year near 4.63% and the ten-year yield index near 4.975%, gains of roughly four and three basis points. Crude fell, with WTI near 99.99 and 2.43% lower, although it held a weekly gain close to 9.7%. Equities rallying while yields rose and crude fell is a two-sided configuration, and conflicting signals are treated here as a stress and confidence input rather than a tail amplifier.

One development is genuinely new and unresolved. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed a precautionary shutdown of the East-West pipeline, a route of roughly 7 million barrels per day that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, following multiple strikes on Thursday in the Riyadh and Madinah regions; technical teams are assessing the line and no restart timeline has been published. Separately, reporting indicates Oman is seeking to convene Gulf Cooperation Council and Iranian foreign ministers in Salalah on Monday. Crude nevertheless fell on the day, which suggests the diplomatic channel was weighed against the outage rather than supply being repriced in one direction.

The forward horizon is dominated by market structure rather than by risk. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, beyond the end of this window, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market. Conditional tail is published at a 5 to 7 residual floor across that stretch and the mode is normal, because the amplifiers that would justify a higher reading, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or price holding at session extremes, all require an open tape. Stress decays from 68 to a weekend baseline near 44, a level held well above zero and above the baseline used before the close, to represent carried exposure into a week containing retail sales, the rate decision with projections, the Monday Hormuz meeting and an unquantified bypass outage.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 21:00 UTC on 10 September to 20:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 18 with the mode event/whipsaw around the previous cash close, then eases through the overnight to a low of 11 as Asian and early European trade stayed orderly. The mode turns trend-up from 06:00 UTC through 11:00 UTC while the European session built a directional advance without denying retracement, with tail contained between 13 and 15. The only watch-band readings are 21 and 22 in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, both marked event/whipsaw around the 12:30 UTC consumer price release, where confidence also fell to 70 and 80 while the outcome was still being absorbed. From 14:00 UTC the series returns to the low band and the mixed mode, holding 13 to 17 through the U.S. afternoon as price rotated beneath an unbroken high, and the final slot covering the cash close reads 13. Stress is the one genuinely elevated series across the window, starting at 86 and declining steadily to 72 by the last slot, the signature of a difficult but recoverable environment rather than a lethal one.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC, and the contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly two hours after this horizon ends. Conditional tail opens at 7 in the current slot, which is the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then settles on a 5 to 6 residual floor for every remaining hour. That floor is model uncertainty rather than a forecast of structure, because a persistent no-retracement price path cannot form while the contract is not trading, and the dominant mode is therefore published as normal across the whole window. No danger window is named, since a narrow evidence-based window requires an open tape. Stress declines from 68 through the fifties to a weekend baseline of 44, deliberately above the 32 used before Friday's close because carried exposure now includes the unresolved East-West pipeline outage on top of a largely closed Hormuz, record distillate prices and a rate decision that is close to fully priced. Confidence decays from 89 to 70 purely as a function of evidence age, since the newest verified observations are the 20:00 UTC cash close and the final futures tick, and nothing inside the horizon can refresh them. The genuine checkpoints all sit beyond this window: the Sunday reopen, the reported Monday Gulf-Iran meeting on the Strait of Hormuz, Tuesday's Empire State survey, and Wednesday's retail sales, rate decision and press conference.
